classification.difficultyReason: Construct a similarity proof using alternate angles formed by intersecting transversals and parallel lines.

content.prompt:
When two intersecting transversals join parallel lines, two triangles are formed.
Explain why these two triangles are similar. Show full reasoning.

spec.description: Two complete horizontal parallel lines, with intersecting transversals B–E–H and G–E–C. All nine point labels and matching single parallel marks are retained. Decorative blue source strokes become house black.
spec.mathematics: A, B, C, D are collinear in that order; F, G, H, I are collinear in that order; AD is parallel to FI. E is the intersection of BH and GC.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens appear in the question diagram; angle equalities and the similarity conclusion belong to the answers.

answer.short: $\triangle BEC\sim\triangle HEG$: $\angle CBE=\angle EHG$ and $\angle BCE=\angle EGH$ (alternate angles on parallel lines). At least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$\angle CBE=\angle EHG$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$\angle BCE=\angle EGH$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

Therefore $\triangle BEC\sim\triangle HEG$, since at least two pairs of corresponding angles are equal (AAA).

Alternatively, $\angle BEC=\angle GEH$ (vertically opposite angles) can be used with either alternate-angle equality; this third equality is optional.
